gen.title: How SI base units build on fixed constants
gen.orderNote: Units appear in page order each later definition builds on earlier constants.

steps.label: Establish the second from cesium frequency
steps.quote: The second is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the cesium frequency ∆νCs, the unperturbed ground-state hyperfine transition frequency
steps.orderHint: Second is defined first as the time base.

steps.label: Define the meter using speed of light
steps.quote: The meter is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the speed of light in vacuum c to be 299,792,458 when expressed in the unit m s^−1
steps.orderHint: Meter uses the already defined second.

steps.label: Define the kilogram using Planck constant
steps.quote: The kilogram is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Planck constant h to be 6.62607015 ×10^−34 when expressed in the unit J s
steps.orderHint: Kilogram builds on meter and second.

steps.label: Define the ampere using elementary charge
steps.quote: The ampere is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the elementary charge e to be 1.602176634 × 10^−19 when expressed in the unit C

steps.label: Define the kelvin using Boltzmann constant
steps.quote: The kelvin is defined by taking the fixed numerical value of the Boltzmann constant k to be 1.380 649 ×10^−23 when expressed in the unit J K^−1
steps.orderHint: Kelvin builds on kilogram, meter and second.

steps.label: Kilogram meter and second together
steps.quote: where the kilogram, meter and second are defined in terms of h, c and ∆νCs.
steps.orderHint: Later units reference the first three units and constants.
